steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Thank you for the generous invitation, Talulah.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: I understand it's hard for your farm to take in so many residents and miners at once.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Taking in some non-Infected is also a dilemma for your people.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: But please trust me when I say we are all skilled workers. We need only shelter to be self-sufficient, and we'll take care of anyone who needs our help.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'm not worried about your people at all. I saw what they can do in Zelgrad, Tulin—I mean, Milana.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Sorry, it'll take some time for me to get used to it.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: No, I should be the one apologizing. I took up that name myself, causing such a long misunderstanding.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: So, the reason you've brought me over here for a chat is...?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: To discuss what to do next... discuss our future.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I once fought the imperial army in the countryside by scattering their forces, and I was sure this was the best way to deal with them.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: But we were naive and disorganized then. Some of us lost our convictions, and some went astray... most of them are dead now.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: We enjoyed a relatively peaceful period after... I spent my days wondering if we could shore up our numbers, tighten our bonds, and hold onto our original ideals—

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: If we can let all Infected... no, all our comrades believe in a better future, have everyone share the same dream, perhaps things could be different this time?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: We've found the enemy we must defeat, and now, we need to gather more comrades to our cause.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: I'm glad to hear that, but I can't help but feel a little regret.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: I'm sad Tulin never got to meet you.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I would be ashamed to meet him, Milana...

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I heard plenty of your stories from Lyudmila... we walked similar paths, experienced similar suffering, but you've done much better than I.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You've never fallen to despair.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: I'm sorry, but I don't quite get you...

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Isn't Reunion a group of strong warriors who have fought their way here? Why would you say something like that...?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'll tell you what happened, if I get the chance.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Anyway, Milana. If you are willing to continue down this path of resistance to the injustices of the empire... let us journey, side-by-side.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: I would be honored.
The youth steps forward and grabs Talulah's hand.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Though, I only know your name, your team—

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: They have no name... we never had the time to work one up.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: But I hope we can work under Reunion's name, if you'd let us.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Don't get me wrong, it's not that I want to permanently borrow someone else's name.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: No, I'm just worried... Reunion has a past full of mistakes. Perhaps our name might cause some more misunderstandings.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Do you still remember, Talulah? When I told you how the most depressed miners would surge back to life upon hearing your stories.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: Even in Zelgrad, an affluent city in the south, there are still people who act in your name to bolster their voices.

steps.name: Milana
steps.text: If we want a name inspiring enough to unite those in pain and frighten those oppressors, our only option in this country is Reunion.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Perhaps...

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: Talulah, I finally found you—

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Hold on, we aren't done talking just yet.

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: Forgive me, but it's urgent news from the south—

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: Something's happened on our farm.
Under the gloomy sky, a fierce fire rages.
First, the barn roof flies into the sky, but before the wooden frame touches the ground, another shell smashes through the barn, flipping barrels by the well...
Over the distant hillside, cannons flash and flicker, like matches being lit, one after another.

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: Enemy artillery! Everyone hide, and fast—

Another barrage of shelling hits the field even before that shout could finish. Splintered wood and dirt rain down as burdenbeast herds neigh alongside children crying, their long period of peace ripped apart.

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: Wh-What's going on...?
Don't panic, just think what you should be doing now!

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: Nine! You're here!

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: I've brought reinforcements, and more hands for evacuation efforts.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Go and see if we've missed anyone who needs help moving. Get them all out, then evacuate at once.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: We'll hold them off, no matter who they are!

steps.name: Reunion Member
steps.text: Right!

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: I'm terribly sorry, Mr. Bułka. Please keep your distance from us, and join the evacuation team for now.

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: This is for your safety.

steps.name: Kazimierzian Merchant
steps.text: Alright, Nine. For, ah—

steps.name: Kazimierzian Merchant
steps.text: We, we're willing to continue our discussion, and trade if you can—

steps.name: Nine
steps.text: Someone, take him away!

steps.name: Kazimierzian Merchant
steps.text: A-Alright, I'll go, I'll go now...
Nine and the Reunion warriors following her arrive in the center of the farm, looking upwards at the massive infantry force rushing down the hill.
Before her blossoms a sea of blood-red flowers, surging towards their enemies.

steps.name: Radioman
steps.text: Sir! Two telegrams just came through.

steps.name: Stern Officer
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Radioman
steps.text: The first: a protest from Kazimierzians. There is fighting on the Ursus-Kazimierz Border, and there's already—

steps.name: Stern Officer
steps.text: Enough. No need to concern ourselves with the Kazimierzians, next.

steps.name: Radioman
steps.text: Sir... this is from headquarters. The Marshal is still recovering from her wounds, but is very satisfied with your progress, and hopes to see the Ursine banner flying over the traitors' base as soon as possible.

steps.name: Stern Officer
steps.text: Heh, we should have done this much sooner... Send a reply: we will fly the flag of the First Army alongside the flag of Ursus.

steps.name: Stern Officer
steps.text: I will show every citizen of our country the most glorious army on this land.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: The most glorious army, huh...?
I know Father and Mother were not buried together.
Father is interred in the royal mausoleum, while Mother is buried in the apple orchard of the summer palace, in a small graveyard at the end of the rows.
...I couldn't possibly have hidden this fact from my mind by simply refusing to think about it.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: This... is not an apple orchard.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty, this was on my mind as well.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: During the reign of the last Tsar, there was a rust sickness outbreak, so the original trees were removed and replaced with other varieties.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: This happened before you were born.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: So the grave on the side here...

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Who does it belong to?

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: ...I did my investigation before you decided to come, and found no one in the palace records. The grave is much smaller than what one would expect for a royal tomb.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: According to tradition, what is buried below may be a beloved pet—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: No. Even a pet would have a name. But this grave lacks one.
Only a single inscription is carved upon the stone.
'For my eternal love. Here I lay to rest in peace her soul.'
Inside the cemetery, a small, simple gravestone leans upon an ornate, royal tombstone, like a child nestling in its mother's arms.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Dig it up.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: ...I beg your pardon?

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: I said, dig out the coffin inside the grave!

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Majesty!

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: Whatever it is you are trying to prove, this is only a fake. It can only be a fake.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: What are you saying?

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: An unidentified individual claiming to be a Grand Princess has appeared in Bresk, with the Grand Duchess's clear support.

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: This is proven by her first appearance in the city to appease the masses, but there is one thing our spies have so far failed to understand.

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: That this 'princess' has made no effort to conceal her face, and according to witnesses...
The usually frank servant suddenly pauses. She looks up at the Tsar to observe his expression, as if unsure if she should continue.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Out with it.

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: Her face is a picture-perfect replica of the late tsarina's.

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: In Bresk and the Far North, practically every household has a 'Red Corner', where they display portraits of the late tsar and tsarina.

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: You need only see and hear her, and witness her 'divine' gifts...

steps.name: Respectful Servant
steps.text: It was but a matter of time before word of this false Grand Princess reached the capital.

steps.name: Witte
steps.text: There are no princesses of Ursus, the late Tsar had no other children. You must know this truth better than anyone else, otherwise all our efforts will have been in vain—

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Do not make me repeat myself, Witte.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: Open it, even if it's just for my sake alone...
The coffin was buried in a shallow grave—one man is enough to haul it up.
It opens to a question. The small box, enough only to house a pet or young child, is completely empty.
No remains nor any belongings are inside.
Nothing at all.
The Tsar approaches the coffin and gets down on one knee, reaching out to rub the surface.
Finally, he spots a name engraved upon it.

steps.name: Fyodor
steps.text: ...'Anastasia Vladimirovna Lacitsara'.
Anastasia.
Sister.
Nastya.
He looks up at the yellow-green leaves and branches, growing from the trees—none of them apple trees.
If the dead are not dead, if vivid memories can be wrong, if forgotten history can be recovered, then...
What other impossibilities lie in wait?

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: ...This will do.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: 'Two meters long, one-and-a-half meters wide, one-and-a-half meters deep.'

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: All the land that a person needs their entire life. So this is what it looks like.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: I don't have a coffin, but this will fit one woman.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: And only one.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: How I wish... I could just stay here with you. To dig another hole next to yours, to lie down and close my eyes, to keep you company forever.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: But I can't. I know where Lada is now, so I have to follow those people to find her.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: Oh, yes. I never got to tell you...

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: I heard Lada's voice on our frequency.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: She's grown, and she remembers everything... she remembers every story we told her. She recognized them immediately!

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: She's so smart... she takes after you.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: I know, you want to go back to Chernobog, but I can only bring you here for now.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: Wait until I see Lada again. I'll bring her here to see you.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: And then, together...

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: We'll go home.
'...General Afanasy Igorevich Khratov, former commander of the Sixth Army's First Division and chief of staff.'
He first distinguished himself in the battle of the Four Emperors, and in the Tenth Ursus-Kazimierz War, led a small elite force to thwart the enemy's counterattack, a rare feat amongst his peers.'
'Later, he demonstrated exemplary prowess in both border and local conflicts with his considerable expertise in combat, raid, suppression, and mediation operations.'

'He learned from his defeat on the Bloodpeak Campaign, and in the Great Rebellion, led his troops away from the Sixth Army and surrendered to the State Council, all to buy more crucial time for a later counterattack...'

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: What are you up to, General?

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Nothing, just reading.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: What's the book?

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Just something a friend returned to me. Are you interested?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Not itching to read it... I remember you having a thread-bound book no one was allowed to touch, and this one is in even worse condition.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: They have similar content.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: You can have this one, if you like.
In between his words, Hellagur swiftly lifts the book to show her the cover, while simultaneously ripping out the page he just read, crumpling it into a ball in his palm.
The already fragile book shakes only slightly, instead of falling apart.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: ...Let's just say I haven't given up yet, General.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: We have a moment's pause for now, but there are even bigger waves about to roll in.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: So I must ask again. You have seen so much more in recent days, yet you're still unwilling to return to our side?

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: What if—what about returning to a brand new Ursus?

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: That's not the main point, Eloysius.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: I refuse, because I know deep inside this place is no longer my home.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Well. Could I please ask you to accept this book at least?

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: From my father's... the Vice Chairman's collection. He always wanted to 'return it to its rightful owner'.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Of course, this is also a thank-you gift, for your help.

steps.name: Eloysius
steps.text: Thank you for bravely defending me, Gospodin Hellagur.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: The Endless March...? A novel? Or is this a history book?

spans.text: ...? A novel? Or is this a history book?

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: You can decide that yourself.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: The pages are practically falling out. Can I really borrow it?

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Alright... thanks.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Oh yeah, almost forgot what I came here for. The Zelgrad group's back, and wanted an office gathering before they leave Ursus. Will you come?

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: When?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Tonight.

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: Alright. I will be there.

steps.name: Voice from Outside
steps.text: ...Who are you looking for?

steps.name: Voice from Outside
steps.text: Just go in and ask...

steps.name: Gentle Youth
steps.text: Excuse me...

steps.name: Gentle Youth
steps.text: Is Vetochki, the miner from the citizen's forum here?

steps.name: Hellagur
steps.text: I've seen you before. Who might you be?

steps.name: Gentle Youth
steps.text: Oh, I...

steps.name: Gentle Youth
steps.text: (Whispers) I'm also a miner, a survivor from the Far North.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: ...It's snowing again.

steps.name: Voice Behind the Door
steps.text: Who knows how many more in the capital will freeze to death tonight.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: You will not manage to save them all, no matter what you might have in mind.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: I should have known how much pride you've always had in yourself. Likewise, I will always be proud of you, Elotta.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: How excellent you are, that I forgot to teach you the most fundamental principle.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: This land has its own rules, and no one can change them by willpower alone.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: The late Tsar failed, and as for our reigning Tsar and Witte... only failure awaits them in turn.

steps.name: Voice Behind the Door
steps.text: Should I take it that you're happy to see them fail?

steps.name: Voice Behind the Door
steps.text: And only with their failure, can you protect your own interests. But whose interests are you actually protecting, with the order you endorse?

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: I see you've forgotten, but the very 'people with something to gain' you're scoffing at were the same ones protecting those Infected from the Far North, and you.

steps.name: Voice Behind the Door
steps.text: So you see it as a sort of charity, and not an innate right?

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: I see it as just a slogan that sounds correct, but has absolutely no substance.

steps.name: Voice Behind the Door
steps.text: No... I'm completely wrong, while you're absolutely right—someone who stays still will never make any mistakes.

steps.name: Voice Behind the Door
steps.text: Chairman Witte and the others will do wrong, because they're trying to do something, trying to change, to stop something.

steps.name: Voice Behind the Door
steps.text: Why see compromises and appeasements as wise decisions, when staying stagnant has never been a difficult choice?

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Still you try to fight reality with naive arguments... it's a habitual mistake, but a mistake of mine too.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Tomorrow I will bring you out of the city, but until then, just stay here and calm down.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: Reflect on your rash actions and the disastrous consequences they're bringing onto the monarch you serve, as well as your family.

steps.name: Voice Behind the Door
steps.text: Father.

steps.name: Voice Behind the Door
steps.text: Do you still think me the girl who trembles at the mere mention of 'confinement' or 'reflection'?

steps.name: Voice Behind the Door
steps.text: You know well I grew out of that long ago.

steps.name: Voice Behind the Door
steps.text: I came back to see you again, because I wanted to. And now...

steps.name: Voice Behind the Door
steps.text: Since you remain obstinate, there are some matters I'll have to take into my own hands.

steps.name: Vasily
steps.text: —Elotta!
The evening breeze lifts the tattered curtains, revealing fresh footprints and bloodstains on the window frame.
Outside the broken window, the twin moons hang high in the night sky, as they always have.
But in the next moment, change occurs. Surprising, silent change.
Streetlights gradually flicker to life on the cold streets.
Lanterns from residences follow after.
Warm lights brighten, one-by-one, gradually blanketing the entire city. Like a palette daubed with bright colors, or a restarted heart beating again.

steps.name: Excited Child
steps.text: Mama, there's light!

steps.name: Excited Child
steps.text: The new year lights on the tree are lit up too!

steps.name: Relieved Civilian
steps.text: Silly... I hear even the electric heaters are running again.

steps.name: Relieved Civilian
steps.text: Don't run about now, we got our bread. Let's go home quickly.

steps.name: Excited Child
steps.text: Now we won't be cold, even if it snows!

steps.name: Relieved Civilian
steps.text: Now we won't be cold, even when the snow melts.
Cheerful laughter accompanies the lights turning on, filling the cold night with warmth.
Only the grand Amber Palace is left in the silent, long darkness.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: ...Alita.

steps.name: Klim
steps.text: Have I done what you wanted to do?

options: Are you sure you want to do this?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Why not?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You may have temporarily stabilized the Sarcophagus, but you need some assistance to turn it into a stable energy source.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: AMa-10's core code can be permanently stored here as an administrator program.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: From another angle, the Sarcophagus is indeed a fitting tomb for the name of AMa-10.

options: Sounds like a coincidence.
A new story always begins from here.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, I've had many links to this Sarcophagus in my long past. Many times I have hidden its existence from civilization.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Until the last time, when I chose to trust someone... and you know the outcome was not ideal.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I remember my words, the last time when we sealed this Sarcophagus together.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If they are truly able to reactivate it, I am willing to believe that it will only be reactivated by someone who's kind in nature.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The future is in the hands of those who seek to truly change this world.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Now, we are indeed faced with the choice once more—to cooperate with all civilizations upon this land, or to go it alone.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I will not deny our current choice is akin to a desperate gamble. I cannot judge it with reason, but we no longer have time.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Instead of being stubbornly conservative... we choose to stand on the side of 'hope'.

options: Sounds like you've let go of some burdens.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Based on the information I've gathered, it seems like you have made the same choice.

options: But this also means...
You won't get a next 'life'.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Isn't that great?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Having but one life, enough to live as a human—is this not a gift from fate?
Distant gunfire ceases, smoke slowly dissipates. Once again the setting sun bathes the broken city in a red glow.
You hear all armies have agreed to a temporary ceasefire, which means the people will have time to evacuate, for now.
So, you embark on your way home.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: So you're saying the Sarcophagus is a stable power source now? I guess Ursus's energy crisis will be somewhat alleviated.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We've done our part for Grypherburg, so we can say our mission's complete, right?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Even if they manage to draw out the Sarcophagus's energy, I fear it'll only be enough for a few nomadic cities in central Ursus to last through this winter.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: They still have a tough problem to solve in the long run.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We can only hope, that the sealed Sarcophagus here won't trigger any more unnecessary conflict...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But Dr. Kal'tsit is back, and all of us are still here too. This mission has been a great success.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: You're right! We got Kal'tsit back! A total Rhodes Island victory!

options: We did what we could.
And from the results, we did pretty well.

steps.text: You look to Kal'tsit, walking behind you.

options: Kal'tsit?
How are you feeling?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I think... I've remembered many things, from a long, long time ago.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: About the Sarcophagus, as well as people and business related to it... only now can I consider those matters to have reached an outcome.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Some memories are so distant they seem to be fading from my mind, which is a new feeling for me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Breathing like this... is suddenly a strange, novel feeling.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Kal'tsit! If you don't feel well, I can hold you, just like before—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No... Thank you, I'm fine.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I will get used to it... as I am now.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...as I will live this life of mine.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, I need you to explain why you asked me to come here as soon as possible.

options: Be patient.
We'll be there soon.
Closure spent a long time preparing for this reunion.
Hopefully, you'll be pleasantly surprised.
Welcome back to Rhodes Island.
Speechless?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It is indeed more magnificent than I imagined.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...You did it, all of you.

options: Just like you said, Rhodes Island will not stop because of the loss of any one person.
Although we hope from the bottom of our hearts that no one will be lost in the first place.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The device here... a regional Originium stasis machine?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Is this the result of new Rhodes Island's research?

options: We put in a lot of work.
To make sure that accident won't happen again.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: An admirable result... but I fear this will not be enough to fend her off completely.

options: We still don't know her true aim...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, I just thought of something else.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In Zelgrad, you found AMa-10's core code in the Sarcophagus's control program.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: AMa-10 was originally designed with access privileges to manage all kinds of devices from the previous civilization, but this function was ultimately not implemented.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In other words... the code within the Sarcophagus was planted by her after waking up.

options: Why would she do that?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If I were to make a reasonable guess, the next step of her plan involves more legacies left by the previous civilization.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We may not know what exactly she's planning, but we have reason to believe she can do far more than what she has done, if she merely wanted to devastate the current civilization on this land.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What you have experienced, is a proof that she is more observer than participant on this Terra.

options: Actually, I heard her voice in a mine, in the Far North.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A debate that has lasted for millennia, a debate about civilization itself.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Now, there is only one thing left to do...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Prove to her—that the civilization on Terra today has the potential to survive, that it has value.

options: We choose to accept this invitation.

steps.name: Borislav
steps.text: Hierda... where are we headed?

steps.name: Borislav
steps.text: Many of my companions are scared. No one's been well since the atrocities in Zelgrad, should we just leave Ursus...?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: We...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I don't think any suffering has to be inevitable. The pain imposed upon us is something that we should fight with all our strength.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: To help those who are suffering and defeat the ones inflicting the suffering... that's what we should do.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Someone once told me of her dream, of her vision for this land... when people will overcome their differences, and Terra becomes a home for everyone.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There may be no end to suffering, but hope continues to live on.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: No, we won't be leaving yet, for now.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: There are still many of our people here suffering, awaiting salvation, and we can't abandon them.

steps.name: Borislav
steps.text: Peter! Why did you—

steps.name: Borislav
steps.text: The spots! You caught it too?!

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: Yeah... *cough* *cough* Couldn't dodge it in the end.

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: It's fine... leave me... I'm gonna die anyway—

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Don't worry... we never leave any of ours behind.
Hierda reaches out, manifesting a pure Originium cluster from thin air in her palm.
Then, she inserts it into the Infected's heart.

steps.name: Despairing Infected
steps.text: Ughh—!

steps.name: Borislav
steps.text: Hierda! What are you—
Blood gushes from the wound, but only for a brief moment.
Soon, crystals spread all over. They cover his wound, then his entire body, and new flesh grows from the Originium.
A brand new body.

steps.name: No Longer Despairing Infected
steps.text: I... The pain, seems to be gone.

steps.name: No Longer Despairing Infected
steps.text: Am I... reborn?
It's a miracle! Hierda has shown us another miracle!
The crowd cheers, then bows and kneels before her.
The girl also gets to her knees. She clasps her hands and prays toward the distant sky.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: God... please, tell me...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Is suffering truly the only law of this world?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Poor child... How do I even break it to you?

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Pain in the mind always stems from a flawed perception of reality.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: But this is an eternal chasm between individual life and this universe, and also an unavoidable divergent path for civilization, that no one can escape.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: Though, not for long.

steps.name: Priestess
steps.text: I will find the answer for you all.
Immersed in the bright light of the twin moons, she casts her gaze to the depths of the ocean.
